labels.note: Where Object.hasOwn exists the fallback behaves the same; without it, hasOwn is undefined and calls crash. Only legacy runtimes.
Fallback only runs when Object.hasOwn is missing; there it would always return false. Needs a legacy-environment test.
A path with no dot splits to one key; pop leaves keys empty, so reduce returns object. Same result.
indexOf('') is always 0, so the condition is always true. Same as the if(true) case, which is equivalent.
Paths with a dot at index 1, like 'a.b', skip nesting and set a flat key 'a.b'.
Type is stored under the '' key; breaks consumers reading __caslSubjectType__ and objects that already have a '' property.
Recasting to a different type throws a TypeError 'Cannot redefine property' instead of the descriptive Error; same type is fine.
Only the exception message text changes.
